title: September Routines
author: Jo Morgan
summary: Jo Morgan walks through the concrete start-of-year systems her maths department runs each September, offered as a template other departments or schools can borrow directly. She covers classroom routines, including a slide displayed every lesson while students pack up so expectations become automatic over time, and a corridor-etiquette poster timed to launch a couple of weeks in rather than day one, to avoid overloading students with information. She describes relaunching the department's homework platform (Sparx) every single year rather than assuming returning students remember how to use it, with a full dedicated lesson for Year 7 and shorter refreshers for older years. She details how the department launches its student support offer through posters, lesson slides, tutor-time notices, and a letter home, with Morgan personally presenting to Year 11 parents at Raising Achievement Evening. Finally, she describes writing a long annual letter to parents across Key Stage 3 and 4 (and, new this year, Year 12) covering FAQs like setting, equipment, and homework, arguing that even though not every parent reads it, providing the information upfront reduces individual email queries throughout the year.
points: Morgan deliberately delays launching her corridor-etiquette poster by a couple of weeks rather than day one, reasoning that students already face information overload at the very start of term.
She relaunches the department's homework platform (Sparx) every single year for every year group, arguing that assuming continuity of platform knowledge is a common and avoidable mistake.
Her student-support launch uses a coordinated multi-channel push, posters, lesson slides, tutor-time notices, screens, and a letter home, rather than relying on any single announcement.
She frames her long annual parent letters as a workload-reduction tool: upfront answers to common FAQs reduce the volume of individual parent emails teachers otherwise field throughout the year.
quotes: No matter how much preparation work I do over the summer holidays, the first two weeks of September always feel insanely busy and stressful.
It's important to set behaviour expectations at the start of the year with every class, not just with new Year 7s.
I decided to wait a couple of weeks to launch this because students already experience information overload at the start of the year.
This seems like an obvious thing to say, but I know that many schools don't do it: I think it's vital to relaunch your homework platform every year.
Admittedly these letters are rather long so I know that some parents won't read them, but I do always get some parents thanking me for providing the information upfront.

The letters cover all the frequently asked questions... which will (hopefully) reduce workload for my team throughout the year because teachers won't get individual emails from parents asking about these things.
